what: Provenance for the experimental structures behind the transcription + splicing view (app/public/struct/polii.json and spliceosome.json). All geometry is derived from these deposited models; no coordinates were invented or modelled by us. Show this when the 3D view displays a polymerase or a spliceosome.
license: PDB data are freely available (wwPDB; no restrictions on use or redistribution).
attribution_line_short: Mammalian Pol II elongation complex, PDB 6GMH (Vos et al., Nature 2018); human spliceosome C* complex, PDB 5XJC (Zhang et al., Cell 2017); human U1 snRNP with a 5' splice site, PDB 4PJO (Kondo et al., eLife 2015) - PDB data are freely available

asset_format.name: utr-race/struct-v1
asset_format.note: Same format as app/public/struct/43s.json, produced by a different pipeline (pipeline/structures_txn/). Read a file as {format, meta, geometry}.
asset_format.meta: pdb_id, title, method, resolution_A, resolution_method, organism, organism_note, state, citation(+citation_fields), doi, pubmed, url, cif_url, license, generated, generated_by, units, origin, origin_in_cif_frame_A, orientation, rotation_matrix_row_major, parts_mapping{rule, parts{<part>:{chains, n_chains, n_residues_modelled, trace_step, entity_descriptions}}, parts_absent}, dimensions_nm, caveats
asset_format.geometry: traces[] (one per continuous modelled stretch: chain, part, label, atom, step, res_first, res_last, n, xyz flat polyline in Angstroms at 0.1 A precision), traces_note, surface_spheres{note, stride, count, xyzr flat [x,y,z,r] quadruples in Angstroms}, plus one structure-specific path block: `transcription_bubble` in polii.json, `splice_sites` in spliceosome.json
asset_format.units: Angstroms everywhere except keys ending in _nm
asset_format.orientation_convention: p_out = R @ (p_cif - origin): translate by the asset's origin, then rotate by rotation_matrix_row_major (3x3, row-major). Translation and rotation only - no scaling, so distances in the files are true physical distances.
asset_format.extra_key: spliceosome.json carries `companion_structures`: [ <a full utr-race/struct-v1 document for PDB 4PJO> ]. It is a SEPARATE structure in its own frame and must not be superposed on the C* complex.

structures.title: Structure of activated transcription complex Pol II-DSIF-PAF-SPT6
structures.organism: Sus scrofa RNA polymerase II; Homo sapiens DSIF (SPT4/SPT5), PAF1 complex and SPT6; synthetic nucleic-acid scaffold
structures.organism_note: MAMMALIAN, NOT HUMAN Pol II. The paper title states 'an activated elongation complex of Sus scrofa Pol II and Homo sapiens DSIF, PAF and SPT6'. Pig Pol II is the standard source for mammalian Pol II elongation complexes; the elongation factors here are human. Label the enzyme 'mammalian Pol II' in the UI, not 'human Pol II'.
structures.state: activated transcription elongation complex (post pause-release), with a complete 48-bp transcription scaffold and nascent RNA
structures.contents: Pol II (12 subunits), DSIF (SPT4/SPT5), PAF1 complex (PAF1, LEO1, CTR9, WDR61, CDC73), SPT6, template DNA, non-template DNA, nascent RNA
structures.why_chosen: A mammalian Pol II ELONGATION complex with a complete 48-bp scaffold: template DNA (48 nt modelled), non-template DNA (37 nt) and nascent RNA (21 nt) are all resolved, so the transcription bubble, the DNA entry and exit duplexes and the RNA exit channel are real geometry rather than a drawing. At 3.1 A it is the highest-resolution mammalian elongation complex with a scaffold this long, and it is the activated (post pause-release) state, which is the state a transcribing polymerase is actually in.
structures.citation: Vos SM, Farnung L, Boehning M, Wigge C, Linden A, Urlaub H, Cramer P. Structure of activated transcription complex Pol II-DSIF-PAF-SPT6. Nature 560:607-612 (2018).
caveats: Coordinates are decimated backbone traces, not full atomic detail.
The enzyme is Sus scrofa (pig) Pol II, not human; the elongation factors are human. Do not label the polymerase 'human' in the UI.
The nucleic-acid scaffold is a synthetic construct used in vitro by the depositors, not a cellular gene.
Part of the single-stranded non-template strand in the bubble (residues 15-25) is disordered and absent from the deposited model, so a bubble drawn from these coordinates alone has a gap.
Only 21 nt of the 46-nt nascent RNA entity are modelled; the RNA emerging beyond the exit channel is not resolved.
The 'clamp' part is an approximate, literature-derived residue range (see meta.parts_mapping.parts.clamp.warning).

structures.title: Cryo-EM structure of the human spliceosome just prior to exon ligation at 3.6 angstrom (C* complex)
structures.organism: Homo sapiens (snRNAs and proteins); pre-mRNA substrate derived from the Human adenovirus 2 major late leader
structures.organism_note: HUMAN spliceosome - no yeast substitution was needed for this asset.
structures.state: C* complex: catalytic step-II-activated spliceosome, after branching (5' exon cleaved, intron lariat formed) and before exon ligation
structures.contents: PRP8, BRR2/SNRNP200, AQR, SNRNP200, RBM22, SLU7, PRP17, PRP22/DHX8, the exon junction complex, Sm cores, 46 protein chains in total, plus U2, U5 and U6 snRNA and the pre-mRNA (18 nt of 5' exon + 66 nt of intron modelled)
structures.why_chosen: A HUMAN spliceosome (no yeast substitution needed) in the C* state: after branching, before exon ligation. The 5' exon, the intron lariat and the branch-point adenosine are all modelled, and the 2'-5' branch can be verified directly in the coordinates (O2' of A144 is 1.63 A from the 5'-terminal phosphorus of intron nucleotide +1), so the branch point in the asset is measured, not assumed. U2, U5 and U6 snRNA are all present.
structures.citation: Zhang X, Yan C, Hang J, Finci LI, Lei J, Shi Y. An Atomic Structure of the Human Spliceosome. Cell 169:918-929 (2017).
caveats: Coordinates are decimated backbone traces, not full atomic detail.
Protein traces use every 3rd CA to keep the file small; do not measure distances along protein traces.
The pre-mRNA substrate is an adenovirus-derived model substrate used in vitro, not a human transcript.
Only 84 of the 275 pre-mRNA nucleotides are modelled (18 exon + 66 intron).
This is one state of a cycle. Do not animate it as if the whole splicing reaction were captured in this one structure.

structures.title: Minimal U1 snRNP (human U1 snRNP bound to a 5' splice site RNA)
structures.resolution_method: X-ray, highest-resolution shell reported by depositors
structures.organism_note: Engineered minimal U1 snRNP: the U1 snRNA four-helix junction is replaced by a kissing loop and stem-loop 4 is shortened. The bound 10-mer 5'-AGGUAAGUCC-3' is a 5' splice site.
structures.state: U1 snRNP with a 5' splice site RNA base-paired to the 5' end of U1 snRNA (the earliest step of splice-site recognition)
structures.contents: U1-70K, U1-C, the seven Sm proteins, U1 snRNA (engineered minimal construct) and the bound 5' splice site RNA
structures.why_chosen: The only step the C* complex cannot show is how a 5' splice site is first recognised. 4PJO is a human U1 snRNP crystallised with a 10-mer 5' splice site RNA (5'-AGGUAAGUCC-3') base-paired to the 5' end of U1 snRNA, which is exactly that step. Included as a companion, in its own frame.
structures.citation: Kondo Y, Oubridge C, van Roon AM, Nagai K. Crystal structure of human U1 snRNP, a small nuclear ribonucleoprotein particle, reveals the mechanism of 5' splice site recognition. eLife 4:e04986 (2015).
caveats: ENGINEERED CONSTRUCT: the U1 snRNA four-helix junction is replaced by a kissing loop and stem-loop 4 is shortened, so this is smaller than a native U1 snRNP. Do not quote its size as the size of U1 snRNP.
U1-A and the SL2 region are not part of this minimal particle.
X-ray structure, so this is a crystal copy, not a particle in solution.
Shown as the step BEFORE the C* complex in spliceosome.json; the two structures are in different coordinate frames and must not be superposed.

rejected_alternatives.title: Cryo-EM structure of Human RNA polymerase II Elongation Complex in an Intermediate Translocation State
rejected_alternatives.citation: Florez Ariza AJ, Lue NZ, et al. Nat Struct Mol Biol (2025).
rejected_alternatives.why_rejected: Genuinely HUMAN Pol II and higher resolution (2.6 A), but the scaffold is short and poorly resolved: only 22 nt of template DNA, 14 nt of non-template DNA and 11 nt of RNA are modelled, so there is almost no upstream or downstream duplex to draw. If the UI must say 'human polymerase', swap to this entry and accept a much shorter DNA.

rejected_alternatives.title: Structure of transcribing mammalian RNA polymerase II
rejected_alternatives.citation: Bernecky C, Herzog F, Baumeister W, Plitzko JM, Cramer P. Nature (2016).
rejected_alternatives.why_rejected: Pol II alone with a 39-bp scaffold - cleaner, but lower resolution and less RNA modelled (14 nt) than 6GMH. A good fallback if the elongation factors clutter the view; 6GMH's `elongation_factors` part can simply be hidden instead.

rejected_alternatives.title: RNA polymerase II elongation complex transcribing genomic DNA extracted from human nuclei
rejected_alternatives.citation: Kujirai T, Kato J, et al. Nat Commun (2025).
rejected_alternatives.why_rejected: Human and high resolution, but a 37-nt scaffold with only 11 nt of RNA.

rejected_alternatives.title: Cryo-EM structure of a human post-catalytic spliceosome (P complex) at 3.0 angstrom
rejected_alternatives.citation: Zhang X, Zhan X, et al. Cell Res (2019).
rejected_alternatives.why_rejected: Higher resolution than 5XJC, but it is the P (post-catalytic) state - the exons are already ligated, so it cannot show splicing about to happen.

rejected_alternatives.title: Cryo-EM structure of a human spliceosome activated for step 2 of splicing (C* complex)
rejected_alternatives.citation: Bertram K, Agafonov DE, et al. Nature (2017).
rejected_alternatives.why_rejected: Same state as 5XJC but at 5.9 A.

unverified: The `clamp` part of polii.json uses RPB1 residues 1-346, the clamp definition for the homologous S. cerevisiae Rpb1 (Cramer, Bushnell & Kornberg, Science 292:1863, 2001) applied to this entry's numbering. We did not validate that mapping against 6GMH, and we could not read that paper's text. Treat it as a highlight, not a domain boundary, and do not print the residue numbers in the UI.

No published transcription-bubble size, DNA:RNA hybrid length, canonical B-DNA rise/twist/diameter, or nuclease-protected nascent-RNA length is quoted anywhere in these files: every publisher page and the Europe PMC full-text endpoint failed (403 / reCAPTCHA / HTTP 500). See txn_constants.json `omitted`.

Resolutions and titles were read from the RCSB REST API (data.rcsb.org/rest/v1/core/entry/<id>); the organism note for 6GMH comes from the abstract of the primary paper, read via the Europe PMC search API.
